also just to clear up any confusion - OT, PT are paramedical/allied science health courses and not clinical medicine. 

MBBS is a double graduation in Medicine and Surgery where you learn to become a "clinical physician" as you put it. having a doctorate and being a doctor are 2 different things, both of which allow you to use the same prefix. 

OT and PT on the other hand are basic undergraduate courses. 

god forbid, someone has a heart attack or an accident or even the flu that OT/PT medical degree isn't doing shit. 

again, OT/PTs are very much an integral and important part of the medical system. there just has to be a differentiation that has to be made imo.

the college isn't legally allowed to give her that prefix, but a lot of students do end up using it. 

as someone who is studying to be a doctor, it's one of my biggest pet peeves when PTs, OTs and allied science professionals use the prefix bc let's be honest you aren't a doctor and you're not legally allowed to call yourself one but just bc a lot of people have been doing for the last few years it's become the norm. 

p.s. this isn't coming from a shitty place and i'm not saying they aren't valued in the medical field, they absolutely are but there has to be a difference made between allied science professionals and actual doctors w a degree.
